name: CA-17
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+21 partisan lean strongly favors Democrats
Khanna's overwhelming financial advantage ($13.8M raised vs. $38K for Tandon)
Incumbent Ro Khanna running for reelection with no serious prior general-election threats
Prediction markets price Khanna at 97% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point decisively to Khanna: a D+21 district, a two-term incumbent with a massive cash advantage, and a challenger who has raised under $40,000. Markets price this race at 97% Democratic, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or unexpected independent expenditure against Khanna is essentially the only path to making this competitive, and none is evident.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ro Khanna seeks another term in this heavily Democratic Silicon Valley district, where the partisan lean is D+21. He advanced to the general election and faces Republican Ritesh Tandon, who has run a minimal campaign with under $40,000 raised and less than $1,000 on hand. Khanna, by contrast, has raised nearly $14 million and holds more than $16 million in cash.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, but prediction markets give Khanna a 97% chance of winning. With no evidence of a competitive race and the challenger lacking resources, this contest sits firmly in Safe D territory.
